note: 'Now the Spirit of God came upon Azariah son of Oded.' (2Chr 15:1).

'When Balaam looked up ... the Spirit of God came upon him' (Num 24:2). **The corpus applies the phrase to a man it elsewhere condemns** -- hired to curse Israel, and named at 2 Peter 2:15 for loving the wages of unrighteousness. The graph records the verse and does not reconcile it.
'Barnabas was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith' (Acts 11:24).

'And I have filled him with the Spirit of God, with skill, ability, and knowledge in all kinds of craftsmanship,' (Exod 31:3), of Bezalel the son of Uri, named at 31:2.

**The first person in the corpus said to be filled with the Spirit, and the gift is craftsmanship.** Not prophecy, not strength, not rule: engraving, and the design of a tent. Repeated word for word at 35:31.
held: inside quoted speech (the Berean's quotation marks), speaker not on record

note:
'While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell upon all who heard his message.' (Acts 10:44), in the house of Cornelius.

**The verse the book turns on.** The circumcised believers are 'astonished ... that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the Gentiles' (10:45), and it is the fact Peter argues from at the Jerusalem council. The Spirit's arrival is used as evidence, not reported as an experience.

'Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the presence of his brothers, and the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon David from that day forward' (1Sam 16:13). **The oil and the Spirit in one verse**, the second following the first, which is where the anointing figure comes from.

His last words claim it again: 'The Spirit of the LORD spoke through me; His word was on my tongue.' (2Sam 23:2).
'When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting ... Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit' (Luke 1:41).

'And the Spirit of the LORD fell upon me and told me to declare' (Ezek 11:5), and it is a recurring event in the book: it enters him and sets him on his feet (2:2), takes him up (3:12), carries him to the valley of bones (37:1). **The only prophet for whom the Spirit is also a means of transport.**

Every one of these says *me*. Ezekiel 1:3 is the frame verse that names him, and it is the only place in the book his name appears. No single verse names them both, which is why this is implied rather than explicit.
'So the Spirit of the LORD came upon Gideon, who blew the ram's horn' (Judg 6:34). One of the few where the person is named in the same clause.
'Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah, and he passed through Gilead' (Judg 11:29). **The verse immediately before the vow**, which the graph records separately and does not connect to this.
'he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother’s womb' (Luke 1:15), spoken by the angel to Zechariah before the birth.
held: inside quoted speech (the Berean's quotation marks), speaker not on record

note: 'The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you' (Luke 1:35) -- **the same verb as the judges, and the only time the corpus uses it of a woman.** Matthew reports the same thing from outside: 'was found to be with child through the Holy Spirit' (1:18).

'As for me, however, I am filled with power by the Spirit of the LORD, with justice and courage' (Mic 3:8). **A claim made in the first person and made against other prophets** -- the surrounding verses are about prophets who divine for money. The prophet is named at Micah 1:1 and nowhere in this chapter, so the identification is a frame and not a statement.
'I will take some of the Spirit that is on you and put that Spirit on them' (Num 11:17). **The Spirit's presence on Moses is stated only in passing, as the source of somebody else's share.**

'The Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he became Israel's judge' (Judg 3:10). The verse says *him*; 3:9 names Othniel the son of Kenaz. **The first of the judges and the first person in the corpus the Spirit comes upon.**
'Then Saul, who was also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, looked directly at Elymas' (Acts 13:9). Ananias promises it at 9:17, in the same breath as his sight.
'Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them, Rulers and elders of the people' (Acts 4:8). The filling and the speech are one sentence, which is Luke's habit throughout Acts.

'the Spirit of the Lord carried Philip away, and the eunuch saw him no more' (Acts 8:39). **Not a filling but a removal** -- the only verse in the New Testament that uses the Spirit the way Ezekiel does.

Four times, and **the only person the corpus says it of more than twice**: it begins to move him at 13:25, comes mightily upon him to tear the lion (14:6), again at Ashkelon (14:19), again at Lehi where the cords fall off (15:14). Every one is physical strength, and nothing else in the corpus uses the phrase that way.

'the Spirit of God rushed upon him, and he prophesied along with them' (1Sam 10:10), promised at 10:6 and repeated at 11:6 when his anger is kindled.

**And then taken away.** 'After the Spirit of the LORD had departed from Saul a spirit of distress from the LORD began to torment him' (1Sam 16:14) -- the verse directly after the one where it comes upon David. The corpus puts the two in consecutive sentences and this edge remains true of 1 Samuel 10, which is the chapter it cites.
'As the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied-but they never did so again.' (Num 11:25), and the same of Eldad and Medad in the camp (11:26).
'the Holy Spirit was upon him' (Luke 2:25), and 'The Holy Spirit had revealed to him that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord’s Christ' (2:26).

'Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit' (Acts 6:5), and at his death 'Stephen, full of the Holy Spirit, looked intently into heaven' (7:55). **Named at his choosing and again at his stoning**, and in Acts the phrase is a description of a man rather than a report of an event.

'select from among you seven men confirmed to be full of the Spirit and wisdom' (Acts 6:3). **Stated as the qualification for the office rather than as an event** -- the only place the corpus makes it a hiring criterion.

'And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit enabled them.' (Acts 2:4), and again at 4:31 after they pray. **The promise of Acts 1:5 reported as kept.**

*The verse says* they, *and the company is larger than this group*: Acts 1:15 counts about a hundred and twenty names. The apostles are the part of it the graph holds, Peter stands up 'with the eleven' to explain what has happened (2:14), and the edge is marked implied because the narrowing is the graph's and not the text's.
'Then his father Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied' (Luke 1:67). **The mute priest, and the filling is what returns his speech to use.**
'Then the Spirit of God came upon Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest, who stood up before the people' (2Chr 24:20). He is stoned in the court of the house of the Lord two verses later.

'After the Holy Spirit had prevented them from speaking the word in the province of Asia' (Acts 16:6), and at Mysia 'the Spirit of Jesus would not permit them' to go into Bithynia (16:7). **Twice in two verses the Spirit's instruction is a refusal**, which is the only place in the corpus it works that way.

'So Barnabas and Saul, sent forth by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia' (Acts 13:4), following 'the Holy Spirit said, Set apart for Me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them' (13:2).
'sent forth by the Holy Spirit' (Acts 13:4). **The sending is stated as the Spirit's own act**, with the church laying on hands at its direction.
